## Triangle inequality · The upper bound {#fv1-triangle .fv-lesson }

```{=html}
<div class="fv-equation"><span data-math="\displaystyle |\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}|\leq|\underset{\sim}{a}|+|\underset{\sim}{b}|"></span></div><div class="fv-triangle-layout"><div class="fv-triangle-diagram" role="img" aria-label="Two vectors placed head to tail form a triangle. Their sum is the straight-line displacement between the endpoints."></div><div><p><strong>The shortest distance between two points is a straight line.</strong></p><p class="small">The direct displacement is no longer than the route along the two vectors.</p><p class="small">Equality holds when non-zero vectors point in the <strong>same direction</strong>.</p></div></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet §1.3 · p. 9</div>

::: {.notes}
Brief explanation only; no routine or controls. The blue resultant is the straight-line route between the same endpoints as the green then gold journey. Connect its length |a+b| to the total length |a|+|b|. Equality occurs for non-zero vectors in the same direction, and also if either vector is zero. This is the upper bound; the lower bound has its own slide.
:::
